subject: Clarification requested: apportionment of availability and partial-degradation credits for Nov 2-3 cascade
messages:
From: Ava Thompson <ava.thompson@acme-eng.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acme-eng.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike Nov 2-3 — request for apportionment of credits

Neha,

We saw a significant increase in tail latency and a small but sustained error-rate increase between 2026-11-02 22:10 UTC and 2026-11-03 04:45 UTC that materially impacted our customer-facing features. Our finance and platform teams are asking for the calculation you use to determine SLA credits in situations where there is a combination of partial degradation (elevated latency but not a full outage) and a downstream vendor (our CDN) experienced a routing flap.

Specifically:
- Region: us-east-1 (most of our traffic)
- Impact window: ~6.5 hours (multiple short spikes within that window)
- Observable: 99th p50-p99 jump from ~200ms to 1.8s, error rates rose to 1.6% from baseline 0.03%
- Business impact: slow page renders for customers and degraded background embeddings calls

Can you confirm how Redwood: 1) attributes availability shortfalls to third-party providers vs Redwood service; 2) treats partial degradation for apportionment (pro-rata by requests, by time, or by error weight); and 3) whether scheduled maintenance windows or overlapping maintenance exempt any portion of the window?

We attached our logs (excerpt) and would like a proposed remediation/credit calculation by early next week so procurement can close the month.

Thanks,
Ava Thompson
Head of Platform, Acme Logistics
[Attachment: acme-uptime-logs.zip (partial logs)]
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Spike Nov 2-3 — request for apportionment of credits

Team — looping you in. Acme (high-revenue, PROD-critical) is asking for how we calculate apportionment when both partial degradation and a third-party CDN flap exist. Kenji copied as well.

Immediate asks:
- PrIyom: can you confirm root cause (Redwood runtime vs external CDN) and provide timestamped metrics for errors, p95/p99, and request volumes.
- Marcus: legal/ops guidance on how we typically apportion credits in mixed-cause incidents; any precedent?
- Marissa: CS lead — please prep the suggested customer-facing language and a conservative credit proposal we can iterate.

Attachments from customer incl. logs. Please reply with notes by EOD so I can get a candidate proposal to Ava Monday.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 13:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike Nov 2-3 — request for apportionment of credits

Quick summary from infra/serving side after initial triage and correlating our traces with CloudEdge status page: 
- Root causes: a CloudEdge routing flap (confirmed 22:05-22:50 UTC on 2026-11-02) caused increased packet loss and TCP retransmits for a subset of edge POPs servicing Acme. During the same broader window (22:10 UTC -> 04:45 UTC) we observed an internal serving pattern: repeated cold-KV-cache churn for embedding flows causing elevated service latencies and some request timeouts.
- Metrics (sampled): 99th latency jump to ~1.8s (22:12-22:48 UTC), error rate peaked 1.6% around 23:05 UTC. Request volume for Acme was within normal band; the impact was higher on background high-concurrency embedding calls.
- Maintenance windows: Redwood had a pre-scheduled minor kernel update earlier that week (10/31 maintenance block) — not overlapping this window. No Redwood-scheduled maintenance during Nov 2-3.

Preliminary engineering view: the incident is mixed-cause. CloudEdge's routing flap amplified request-level retries which in turn exposed an internal cache-regen pattern in our embedding path. If we attributed everything to the CDN it would be inaccurate; likewise saying it's solely Redwood's fault ignores the clear external event.

I attached an incident-timeline.csv with per-minute error and latency counts and our trace links. Will follow up with a per-minute apportionment table for review.

- PrIyom
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident-timeline.csv (per-minute metrics)]
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike Nov 2-3 — request for apportionment of credits

Thanks — I reviewed the timeline. Two points for a conservative, defensible approach we can share with Acme: 

1) Apportionment methodology proposal (recommended):
   - Compute per-minute impact score = (fraction_of_requests_exceeding_SLO * 0.7) + (normalized_error_rate * 0.3).
   - Total creditable impact = sum(impact_score_minutes) / total_minutes_in_billing_period_for_region.
   - For mixed-cause minutes, split responsibility between Redwood and CloudEdge based on signatures in the traces (TCP retransmit rate and 4xx/5xx distribution). If >60% of the failed requests show external TCP retransmits, cap external vendor share at 70% for that minute; otherwise Redwood retains larger share.

2) Policy & precedent: our standard SLA (see clause 4.2 in redwood-sla-policy.pdf) treats vendor-caused outages as exceptions only when the failure is complete and isolated to the vendor's domain with no concurrent internal anomalies. Mixed-cause incidents are explicitly addressed by pro-rata apportionment (time + request-weighted).

Practical suggestion: propose to Acme that Redwood issues an immediate credit equal to 60% of the calculated creditable impact, and we pursue 40% recovery from CloudEdge (or pass-through if CloudEdge accepts). This is defensible, gets cash to the customer quickly, and matches precedent in SUP-4821.

I'll attach a redlined calc and the snippet of clause 4.2 for transparency.

-Marcus
Director, Product Operations
[Attachment: redwood-sla-policy.pdf (excerpt)]
From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Thompson <ava.thompson@acme-eng.com>
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acme-eng.com>, priyom.das@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed apportionment and provisional credit for Nov 2-3 latency cascade

Ava — thanks for the logs and for your patience while we completed an initial analysis. Below is a concise summary and our proposed path forward.

What we found:
- Primary external event: CloudEdge routing flap (22:05-22:50 UTC on 2026-11-02) that affected a subset of POPs serving your traffic (CloudEdge incident: https://status.cloudedge.example.com/incidents/2026-11-02-routing-flap).
- Internal amplification: concurrent KV-cache churn on our embedding path increased request latency and produced some timeouts between 22:10 UTC and 04:45 UTC.

Proposed apportionment approach (short):
- We calculated per-minute impact using a request-weighted latency+error score and apportioned responsibility per-minute between CloudEdge and Redwood based on trace signatures.
- Conservative provisional split: Redwood: 60% of creditable impact; CloudEdge: 40% (we are initiating a recovery request with CloudEdge).

Proposed immediate remedy:
- Redwood will issue a provisional customer credit of $12,500 against the upcoming invoice (representing 60% of the calculated creditable impact). This credit is immediate and not contingent on CloudEdge acceptance. If CloudEdge reimburses us, we will pass through the recovered amount or reconcile on the next invoice per your preference.

Next steps:
1) If this works for Acme, reply to confirm and we will generate a formal credit note.
2) We will produce a joint postmortem and a one-week tactical plan to reduce KV-cache churn sensitivity to vendor-induced retransmits.
3) We will continue to pursue CloudEdge for 40% recovery and share their response/Ticket ID (we opened SUP-4821 for internal tracking).

We want to be fair and fast — open to adjusting the split if Acme has specific data that shifts the minute-level attribution.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-credit-note-draft.pdf (internal)]
From: Ava Thompson <ava.thompson@acme-eng.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Kenji Sato <kenji.sato@acme-eng.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 17:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed apportionment and provisional credit for Nov 2-3 latency cascade

Neha — thank you. We appreciate the quick, pragmatic proposal and the transparency in the methodology. Acme accepts the provisional $12,500 credit and would like the joint postmortem and the tactical plan as part of our operational review next week. Please include the minute-level apportionment CSV in the postmortem so our engineers can validate.

Ava
Head of Platform, Acme Logistics
